raw_segments.text: And King Agamemnon answered, Nestor, if the Trojans are indeed fighting at the rear of
our ships, and neither the Wall nor the Trench has served us, over which the Danons twalled
so hard, and which they deemed would be an impregnable bulwark both for us and our fleet,
I see it must be the will of Jove that the Achaeans should perish ingloriously here,
I knew when Jove was willing to defend us, and I know now that he is raising the Trojans
to like honor with the gods, while us, on the other hand, he is bound hand and foot.
Now therefore, let us all do as I say.
Let us bring down the ships that are on the beach and draw them into the water.
Let us make them fast to their mooring stones a little way out, against the fall of night.
If even by night the Trojans will desist from fighting, we may then draw down the rest of
There is nothing wrong in flying ruin even by night.
It is better for a man that he should fly and be saved than be caught and killed.
